descriptionChirho: To physically crush, break, or bruise something or someone, in the basic Qal active stem.
Passive participle describing the condition of being crushed, bruised, or broken — used adjectivally of objects or persons.
Passive participle used substantivally to denote oppressed or downtrodden people as a social class.
Active participle used substantivally to denote those who crush or oppress others.
Intensive stem conveying deliberate, thorough, or repeated crushing and oppression of persons or things.
Causative stem indicating bringing about the crushing or shattering of something.
Passive or middle voice expressing that the subject is broken, crushed, or shattered, in Nifal and Qal intransitive imperfect forms.
Reciprocal stem describing mutual jostling, struggling, or pushing against one another.
